A-1-X-P.name: Complex Strategic Decision
A-1-X-P.description: Should the company pivot? Should I switch careers? Should the city build a subway?
A-1-X-P.reason: Strategic decisions fear treating symptoms not root causes. Contradiction Analysis finds the real problem (principal contradiction), Strategic Foresight ensures you see beyond the immediate (foresee trends), Systems Thinking prevents tunnel vision (holistic view). All three are indispensable.
steps:
Step 1: List all problems (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Write down all problems and conflicts you face
  -> Don't filter, write everything

Step 2: Distinguish primary/secondary (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Which problem pulls one hair and moves the whole body?
  -> Which problem solved makes others auto-relieve?
  -> That's the principal contradiction

Step 3: Draw the big picture (Systems Thinking)
  -> Map the principal contradiction and all related factors as a relationship diagram
  -> Mark which are positive feedback (amplifying), which are negative feedback (suppressing)
  -> Find the leverage points in the system

Step 4: Simulate the future (Strategic Foresight)
  -> If Option A, what happens in 1/3/5 years?
  -> If Option B, what happens in 1/3/5 years?
  -> List best/worst/most likely for each

Step 5: Decide
  -> Choose the option with clearest principal contradiction and most controllable global impact
  -> Make contingency plans
expected: Decisions shift from gut feel to analysis
See 3-5 years ahead
Know what matters, ignore noise
A-1-X-P.case:
A traditional retailer faces e-commerce disruption.
Contradiction Analysis: Surface problem is online stealing business; principal contradiction is offline cannot provide value that online lacks.
Systems Thinking: Offline assets are space+people+immediacy; online assets are data+scale+convenience.
Strategic Foresight: Pure online gets platform-locked, pure offline slowly dies, integration is the way.
Decision: Transform stores to experience centers, online does data-driven recommendations, offline does experience+delivery. In 3 years, offline experience stores become brand moat.

A-1-X-R.name: Long-term Strategic Layout
A-1-X-R.description: Long-term strategic layout, 10-year corporate plan, 10-year personal growth
A-1-X-R.reason: Long-term layout is about survive and thrive. Protracted War Thinking plans three stages (defense->stalemate->counteroffensive), Encircle Cities from Countryside finds niches giants ignore, Gradual Reform ensures progress each stage.
steps:
Step 1: Assess strength (Protracted War)
  -> Honestly assess resource gap vs opponent
  -> If gap >5x, enter defense stage
  -> If gap 2-5x, prepare stalemate
  -> Only if gap <2x, consider counteroffensive

Step 2: Find weak market (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does opponent serve poorly?
  -> Which customer segments are ignored?
  -> Pick a niche opponent ignores or does badly

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Become #1 in that niche
  -> Accumulate reputation, capital, talent
  -> Don't rush to expand, secure the base first

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate from base to adjacent markets
  -> Each expansion <=50% of current size
  -> New market must be profitable in 6 months

Step 5: Wait for timing (Protracted War)
  -> When you reach 30-50% of opponent size
  -> Opponent notices you
  -> Enter stalemate: defend + accumulate
  -> Keep deepening your advantage areas

Step 6: Counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> When you exceed opponent in a domain
  -> Concentrate resources to attack
  -> One core domain at a time
expected: Foothold in 1 year
Niche advantage in 2-3 years
Capacity to compete head-on with giants in 5 years
A-1-X-R.case:
Pinduoduo rose under Alibaba/JD duopoly.
Encircle Cities: Alibaba/JD focused on tier 1-2 cities, Pinduoduo started from tier 3-4 and rural.
Protracted War: Massive subsidies early, no profit, accumulated users.
Gradual expansion: From agri-products to full category, from sinking market upward.
Result: Became China's 2nd largest e-commerce platform.

A-1-Y-P.name: Business Competition
A-1-Y-P.description: New product launch facing competitors, market share battle, price war
A-1-Y-P.reason: Business competition is not who hits harder, but who thinks smarter. Total Victory Mindset reminds you: best competition is no competition (differentiation), Mental Models help understand competitive landscape from multiple angles, Mobile Warfare says: don't fight every battle, concentrate force on winnable ones.
steps:
Step 1: Know self and enemy (Total Victory)
  -> List your strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> List competitors' strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> Find battles opponent must win but you don't need to

Step 2: Multi-angle analysis (Mental Models)
  -> Economics: supply/demand, marginal cost, network effects
  -> Psychology: user decision biases, anchoring
  -> Ecology: species niches, ecological positioning
  -> Military: center of gravity, supply lines, high ground

Step 3: Find your niche (Total Victory)
  -> Where does competitor perform worst?
  -> Can you be best in that market?
  -> If yes, that's your ecological niche

Step 4: Concentrated attack (Mobile Warfare)
  -> All resources on chosen niche
  -> Become absolute #1 in that market
  -> Don't spread thin to other markets

Step 5: Build moat
  -> Brand, network effects, switching costs as barriers
  -> Make it hard for competitors to enter your niche
expected: Avoid head-on price war
Build absolute advantage in niche
Win by differentiation not attrition
A-1-Y-P.case:
A Chinese phone brand vs Apple/Samsung duopoly.
Total Victory: Don't fight on flagships, start with mid-low end.
Mental Models: Network effects (social), anchoring (value), economies of scale.
Mobile Warfare: Concentrate on camera, become best in price segment.
Result: From low-end to high-end breakthrough.

A-1-Y-S.name: Market Research
A-1-Y-S.description: Pre-entry market research, competitor analysis, user personas
A-1-Y-S.reason: Market research fears subjective speculation. Seek Truth from Facts ensures facts over assumptions, Mass Line ensures hearing real user voices not reports, Abstract Induction extracts core patterns from messy data.
steps:
Step 1: Define research goals (Seek Truth)
  -> Clarify 3 core questions
  -> Set time/budget/sample limits

Step 2: Go to frontline (Mass Line)
  -> Shadow support team 3 days, log complaints
  -> Surveys + deep interviews
  -> Don't ask what you like, ask what pains you most

Step 3: Identify core needs
  -> Top 3 mentioned needs
  -> Filter fake needs (say they want but don't use)

Step 4: MVP development (Gradual Reform)
  -> 2 weeks to minimum viable
  -> Budget <=10% of total
  -> Only core-need features

Step 5: Launch + collect data (Feedback Loops)
  -> Positive feedback (more users->more content->more users)
  -> Negative feedback (more users->noise->quality users churn)

Step 6: Continuous iteration
  -> Weekly small releases
  -> Each version incorporates user feedback
expected: Product-market fit improves
Iteration speed 3x faster
Retention significantly higher
A-1-Y-S.case:
A SaaS company wants AI features but doesn't know what.
Flexible Strategy: List 10 AI scenarios (smart support, auto-reports, recommendations).
Gradual Reform: 2 weeks, 3 MVPs, 50 seed users each.
Natural Selection: Smart reports usage 5x others, highest willingness to pay.
Result: Cut other 2, focus on smart reports, core differentiator in 6 months.

A-1-Y-Q.name: Institution Design
A-1-Y-Q.description: Design performance reviews, promotion mechanisms, corporate governance
A-1-Y-Q.reason: Institution design is not just writing rules, but designing a self-regulating system. Procedural Justice ensures fairness, Game Theory designs incentives, Feedback Loops predicts long-term effects.
steps:
Step 1: Clarify institution goal
  -> What problem to solve? (Incentive? Fairness? Efficiency?)

Step 2: Design process (Procedural Justice)
  -> Nomination->Review->Publicity->Appeal, each step has rules

Step 3: Simulate game (Game Theory)
  -> If institution is like this, how will people respond?
  -> Any loopholes to exploit?

Step 4: Predict feedback (Feedback Loops)
  -> What positive feedback will this trigger?
  -> What negative feedback?

Step 5: Pilot in small scope
  -> One department first
  -> 3 months evaluate, adjust, then scale
expected: Institutional fairness significantly improved
Gaming behavior reduced
Employee satisfaction increased
A-1-Y-Q.case:
A company designs new performance review.
Procedural Justice: Nomination->Review->Publicity->Appeal, each step has rules.
Game Theory: Simulate responses, found collusion loophole, added cross-dept review.
Feedback Loops: Predicted short-termism negative feedback, added long-term incentive weight.
Result: Fairness up, gaming down, satisfaction up.

A-2-X-P.name: Investment Decision
A-2-X-P.description: Whether to invest in a project? How to adjust asset allocation?
A-2-X-P.reason: Investments biggest enemy is yourself. Marginal Thinking helps rational allocation (last dollar ROI), Loss Aversion identifies emotional traps, Dual-System Thinking forces rational analysis on big decisions.
steps:
Step 1: Marginal analysis (Marginal Thinking)
  -> Not total return, but marginal return
  -> Where does last dollar earn highest ROI?

Step 2: Identify emotional traps (Loss Aversion)
  -> Refusing to stop loss because already down?
  -> FOMO chasing highs?

Step 3: Forced cooldown (Dual-System)
  -> Any large investment above threshold: 24hr wait
  -> Write decision rationale AND bear case

Step 4: Diversify + Focus
  -> Core (60%) in most certain direction
  -> Satellite (40%) in high-potential directions
expected: Impulsive trades reduced 70%+
Annual return volatility lower
Decision quality from gut to analysis
A-2-X-P.case:
An investor faces add-to-position decision.
Marginal: Where does last 100k earn best?
Loss Aversion: Found self refusing stop-loss due to sunk cost.
Dual-System: 24hr cooldown, wrote bear case.
Result: Avoided chasing high, bought dip on pullback, 15% better annual return.

A-2-Y-P.name: Negotiation
A-2-Y-P.description: Business negotiation, salary negotiation, M&A negotiation
A-2-Y-P.reason: Negotiation is not who hits harder, but who thinks smarter. Total Victory: best competition is no competition (differentiation), Game Theory designs incentives for cooperation.
steps:
Step 1: Know self and counterparty (Total Victory)
  -> List both strengths, weaknesses, resources
  -> Find what they must win but you don't need to

Step 2: Design mechanism (Game Theory)
  -> If negotiation is this way, how will they respond?
  -> How to structure terms so they feel cooperation is optimal?

Step 3: Design BATNA
  -> Your BATNA (best alternative)?
  -> Their BATNA?

Step 4: Concession list
  -> Things you give cheap but they value high
  -> These are your negotiation chips

Step 5: Concession in steps
  -> Don't show all cards at once
  -> Each concession extracts real counter-concession
expected: Avoid passive acceptance of bad terms
Hold ground on core interests
Build long-term partnership not one-off deal
A-2-Y-P.case:
A company renews contract with major client.
Total Victory: Don't fight on price, trade service upgrade for renewal.
Game Theory: Tiered service + incentive rebate, guides client to long-term.
Result: 3-year renewal, price -5% but total value +30%, both satisfied.

A-2-Y-R.name: Long-term Competition (Resources Tight)
A-2-Y-R.description: Startup vs giant, individual in industry, resource-constrained long competition
A-2-Y-R.reason: Resource-tight long competition is about survive and thrive. Encircle Cities finds niches giants ignore, Guerrilla Tactics enables flexible maneuver, Gradual Reform ensures progress each stage.
steps:
Step 1: Assess strength (Protracted War)
  -> Honestly assess resource gap
  -> Gap>5x: defense
  -> Gap 2-5x: stalemate prep
  -> Gap<2x: counteroffensive prep

Step 2: Find weak market (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does giant serve poorly?
  -> Which customers ignored?
  -> Pick market giant ignores

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Become #1 in niche
  -> Accumulate reputation, capital, talent
  -> Don't rush expansion, secure base first

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate to adjacent markets
  -> Each expansion <=50% current size
  -> New market profitable in 6 months

Step 5: Wait for timing (Protracted War)
  -> At 30-50% opponent size, enter stalemate
  -> Keep deepening advantage areas

Step 6: Counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> When exceeding opponent in a domain
  -> Concentrate resources to attack
  -> One core domain at a time
expected: Foothold in 1 year
Niche advantage in 2-3 years
Head-on capacity vs giants in 5 years
A-2-Y-R.case:
A SaaS startup vs Salesforce monopoly.
Encircle Cities: Salesforce targets enterprise, startup from SMB.
Guerrilla: Free tier early, build user reputation.
Gradual expansion: CRM -> marketing automation, SMB upward.
Result: Vertical #1, acquired by big tech.

A-3-Y-R.name: Breakout from Disadvantage
A-3-Y-R.description: Extremely resource-poor, disadvantaged position, need turnaround
A-3-Y-R.reason: Extreme disadvantage only way out: avoid strength hit weakness, flexible maneuver, self-reliance. Encircle Cities finds gaps opponent ignores, Flexible Strategy adapts fast, Self-Reliance ensures no external bailout dependence.
steps:
Step 1: Admit gap, no head-on
  -> Honestly assess: where absolutely weaker?
  -> Abandon battles you must win but can't

Step 2: Find gaps (Encircle Cities)
  -> Where does opponent serve worst?
  -> Which customers completely ignored?
  -> Pick domain opponent doesn't even care about

Step 3: Flexible maneuver (Flexible Strategy)
  -> No fixed playbook, strike where open
  -> They defend A hard, you attack B
  -> When they react to B, you're already at C

Step 4: Self-reliance (Self-Reliance)
  -> Don't expect external funding/partnership to save
  -> Cash flow must be self-generated
  -> Core tech/capability must be self-developed

Step 5: Accumulate counteroffensive capital
  -> Become #1 in chosen domain
  -> Accumulate cash, talent, tech moats
  -> Wait for opponent mistake or environment shift, then total attack
expected: Foothold in niche in 6 months
Cash flow positive in 1-2 years
Counteroffensive capacity in 3-5 years
A-3-Y-R.case:
Vertical SaaS vs Salesforce.
Admit gap: No full CRM, abandon enterprise.
Find gaps: Focus on medical aesthetics clinic management (Salesforce ignores).
Flexible: Scheduling first, then inventory, then marketing tools.
Self-reliance: Customer prepayments fund ops, no VC.
Result: Vertical #1, reverse entry into general SaaS.

B-2-Y-S.name: Technical Breakthrough
B-2-Y-S.description: Core tech bottleneck, algorithm optimization, architecture refactor
B-2-Y-S.reason: Technical breakthrough is not linear progress, but long accumulation + sudden paradigm shift. Flexible Strategy avoids single-path lock-in, Punctuated Equilibrium reminds breakthroughs come from paradigm shifts, Self-Reliance ensures core tech independence.
steps:
Step 1: Multi-path exploration (Flexible Strategy)
  -> List 3-5 possible technical approaches
  -> Small resource pre-research each
  -> Don't put all eggs in one basket

Step 2: Spot paradigm shift (Punctuated Equilibrium)
  -> Watch new papers, frameworks, hardware
  -> Ask: any new paradigm makes old problem simple?
  -> e.g., Transformer made NLP from RNN obsolete

Step 3: Core self-reliance (Self-Reliance)
  -> Core algorithms/arch must be self-developed
  -> Key dependencies must have fallbacks
  -> Cannot be locked by single vendor/opensource

Step 4: Small fast validation
  -> Minimum prototype each direction
  -> Benchmarks speak, not intuition

Step 5: Focused breakthrough
  -> Resources to most promising 1 path
  -> Concentrate firepower on core challenge
expected: Avoid 6+ months wasted on wrong direction
Core tech self-controlled
Breakthrough speed 2-3x
B-2-Y-S.case:
An AI chip company cracks sparse compute acceleration.
Multi-path: Sparse matrix compression, dynamic pruning, knowledge distillation 3 paths.
Punctuated Equilibrium: Found sparse patterns auto-optimizable by compiler (paradigm shift).
Self-reliance: Core compiler self-built, not dependent on TVM/MLIR upstream.
Result: 60% latency reduction, 3x energy efficiency.

B-1-Z-S.name: Product Rapid Iteration
B-1-Z-S.description: Zero-to-one product, MVP validation, PMF search
B-1-Z-S.reason: Products aren't built in isolation. Flexible Strategy responds fast to market feedback, Feedback Loops builds growth flywheel, Gradual Reform iterates in small steps.
steps:
Step 1: Rapid hypotheses (Flexible Strategy)
  -> 5 core hypotheses (user needs X, pays Y, channel Z)
  -> Sort by validation cost, test cheapest first

Step 2: MVP (Gradual Reform)
  -> 2 weeks to minimum viable
  -> Budget <=10% total
  -> No admin backend, core interaction first

Step 3: Real user test (Feedback Loops)
  -> 20 seed users try
  -> Positive feedback (more users->more value->more users)
  -> Negative feedback (more users->worse exp->churn)

Step 4: Data-driven iteration
  -> Weekly release
  -> Each version changes 1-2 KPI features
  -> A/B test every change

Step 5: Build growth flywheel
  -> Identify loop (acquire->activate->retain->refer->acquire)
  -> Strengthen positive, cut negative
  -> Dashboard with daily north-star metric
expected: MVP live in 2 weeks
PMF validated in 1 month
Iteration speed 3x
B-1-Z-S.case:
Team building AI writing tool.
Rapid hypotheses: Users need outline generation not full text.
MVP: 2 weeks outline generator, 50 seed users.
Feedback Loops: Users love outline->fulltext one-click, 40% retention.
Rapid iteration: 1 template/week, 10k DAU in 3 months.

C-2-Y-P.name: Leadership Development
C-2-Y-P.description: IC to leader transition, new manager adaptation
C-2-Y-P.reason: Good leaders don't manage everything, they manage the right things. Mass Line ensures hearing truth, Wu Wei teaches letting go, Systems Thinking sees org holistically.
steps:
Step 1: Go to frontline (Mass Line)
  -> Half day/week with team
  -> Don't ask what's the problem, ask what blocks you
  -> Log: what makes them feel powerless, waste time, lack support

Step 2: Set goals and standards (Wu Wei)
  -> Only set goals/standards, don't dictate how
  -> Let team find their way
  -> Your job: remove obstacles, not direct moves

Step 3: Draw org map (Systems Thinking)
  -> Mark key roles, dependencies, info flows
  -> Find single points of failure (person leaves = system down)

Step 4: Rotation system
  -> Team members rotate as Tech Lead
  -> Grow next-gen leaders
  -> You gradually exit daily decisions
expected: Team autonomy increases
Leader freed from daily approvals
Org resilience strengthened
C-2-Y-P.case:
Tech director from IC to management.
Frontline: Half day/week code review + sit in meetings, ask what blocks not progress.
Wu Wei: Only set deliver X feature + 80% coverage, no tech direction.
Systems: Drew architecture deps, found auth service as single point, drove refactor.
Result: Team autonomous delivery up, he got time for strategy.

C-2-Z-P.name: Conflict Mediation
C-2-Z-P.description: Team internal conflicts, cross-dept friction, partner disputes
C-2-Z-P.reason: Conflict essence is unmet needs collision. Contradiction Analysis sees through phenomenon to essence, Framing Effect reframes to reduce antagonism, United Front redirects to shared goals.
steps:
Step 1: Separate private talks (Seek Truth)
  -> Talk to each party alone, no stance
  -> Ask: Core demand? Absolute bottom line?
  -> Log both core interests, red lines, emotional triggers

Step 2: Reframe (Framing Effect)
  -> Not who right/wrong, but what shared goal blocked?
  -> A vs B wrong -> we both want success, methods differ
  -> Zero-sum -> positive-sum

Step 3: Open dialogue (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Face to face, you facilitate
  -> Each says: I understand their demand is...
  -> Find principal contradiction (usually 1 core disagreement)

Step 4: Third option (United Front)
  -> Not A compromise or B compromise, but 3rd way
  -> Find common enemy (competitor/deadline/tech debt)
  -> Turn internal conflict into external shared challenge

Step 5: Written agreement
  -> Who does what, deadline, breach handling
  -> Set review checkpoint (2 weeks)
expected: 1-2 sessions resolve most cooperation conflicts
Culture: conflicts can be constructive
Avoid talent loss, project delays
C-2-Z-P.case:
R&D vs Product over frequent requirement changes.
Contradiction: Core issue not many changes, but zero-cost changes.
Reframe: Who right/wrong -> how to make changes orderly.
United Front: Common enemy is delivery delay.
Agreement: Changes need PO sign-off + impact assessment, emergency fast-track with post-fix.
Result: Change throughput 3x, no more antagonism.

C-3-Y-S.name: Interpersonal Relations
C-3-Y-S.description: Workplace conflicts, managing up, cross-dept collaboration
C-3-Y-S.reason: 90% interpersonal issues stem from cognitive biases and framing misalignment. Cognitive Bias Identification reveals blind spots, Framing Effect changes response by changing expression, Dual-System reminds slow thinking before key conversations.
steps:
Step 1: Identify own biases (Cognitive Bias ID)
  -> Interpreting no reply as disrespect? (confirmation bias)
  -> Feeling owed because I gave much? (sunk cost)
  -> Write: how much of my judgment is fact vs inference?

Step 2: Reframe communication (Framing Effect)
  -> Not you always..., but when X happened I felt Y, I hope Z
  -> Accusation -> request, accusation -> shared goal
  -> E.g., you don't support me -> this project matters, I need specific support...

Step 3: Activate slow thinking (Dual-System)
  -> 10 min forced wait before important convo
  -> Write: my goal? their need?
  -> Rehearse: if they refuse, how I respond?

Step 4: Seek win-win
  -> Ask: what outcome good for both?
  -> Propose specific, low-cost, acceptable action
  -> Set review checkpoint
expected: Conflict escalation probability down 80%
Cross-dept collaboration significantly improved
Reusable communication templates established
C-3-Y-S.case:
PM vs designer over design delivery delay.
Bias ID: PM thought designer procrastinating, actually waiting upstream requirements.
Reframe: Why so slow -> we launch Friday, need lock Wednesday, what support you need?
Dual-System: PM cools 10 min, realizes anxiety projection.
Result: Designer delivered Wednesday, project on time.

D-1-Y-R.name: Personal Growth Planning
D-1-Y-R.description: Career planning, skill tree building, side hustle choice, lifelong learning
D-1-Y-R.reason: Personal growth is a marathon. Gradual Reform avoids overcommitment, Mental Models builds cross-domain framework, Natural Selection: try many, fail fast, keep what fits.
steps:
Step 1: Inventory current state (Seek Truth)
  -> Skill matrix: list skills, rate 1-10
  -> Time audit: where did last week go?
  -> Energy audit: what charges vs drains you?

Step 2: Build skill tree (Mental Models)
  -> Core skill (moat): 1 to top 10%
  -> Satellite skills (leverage): 3-5 at standard
  -> New domain exploration: 1 per quarter

Step 3: Small fast steps (Gradual Reform)
  -> Weekly micro-goal (read 1 chapter, write 1 article, practice 1 hr)
  -> Not perfection, done
  -> Retro: what learned this week? what change next?

Step 4: Natural Selection (Natural Selection)
  -> Quarterly review: what compounds? what depreciates?
  -> Keep compounding skills (writing, coding, English, investment thinking)
  -> Cut depreciating/no-feedback investments

Step 5: Build compounding system
  -> Input: 30 min/day high-quality
  -> Process: Feynman/zettelkasten/mindmap
  -> Output: 1 article/week or code
  -> Feedback: collect -> adjust input
expected: Clear skill radar in 1 year
Expert moat in 1 domain in 3 years
Sustainable lifelong learning system built
D-1-Y-R.case:
Programmer wants to pivot to AI.
Inventory: Coding strong, math weak, English average.
Skill tree: Core=Python+DL frameworks, Satellite=math+paper reading.
Gradual: 1hr/day papers+replication, weekend blog retros.
Natural Selection: 3 months quit RL (poor feedback), focus CV.
Result: Top conference paper in 1 year, pivot successful.

D-2-Y-R.name: Organizational Capability Building
D-2-Y-R.description: Engineering systems, R&D processes, talent pipeline
D-2-Y-R.reason: Org capability building is a protracted war. Protracted War stages it (foundation->system->results), Encircle Cities starts from strongest pain point, Gradual Reform ensures each step solid.
steps:
Step 1: Assess current (Protracted War)
  -> Honest eval: eng efficiency, code quality, delivery cycle, talent density
  -> If foundation very weak: defense (stop bleeding)
  -> If foundation okay: stalemate (build system)
  -> If foundation good: counteroffensive (benchmark)

Step 2: Find entry point (Encircle Cities)
  -> Which dept has strongest pain, strongest will, least resistance?
  -> Pick 1 dept as pilot, don't roll out all
  -> E.g., CI/CD in core business team first, then company-wide

Step 3: Build base (Encircle Cities)
  -> Pilot team runs: process, tools, standards, metrics
  -> Output: templates, automated pipelines, quality gates
  -> Verify: delivery faster, defects down, satisfaction up

Step 4: Expand gradually (Encircle Cities)
  -> Radiate from pilot to adjacent teams
  -> Each expansion <=50% current size
  -> New team must run process in 3 months

Step 5: Stalemate and counteroffensive (Protracted War)
  -> At 50% coverage: consolidate + optimize
  -> At 80%+: publish standards, enable others, build brand
expected: Core team runs eng system in 6 months
60%+ teams covered in 1 year
Industry-benchmarkable eng effectiveness in 2 years
D-2-Y-R.case:
Mid-size tech builds eng system.
Protracted War: Don't talk standards first, solve 2hr build pain.
Encircle Cities: Core transaction team pilot, CI/CD to 15min.
Gradual Reform: Pipeline first, then code standards, test coverage gates.
Gradual expansion: 1 team -> 3 teams -> 12 teams.
Counteroffensive: Published Engineering Effectiveness Whitepaper, industry benchmark.

D-2-Z-P.name: Crisis Response
D-2-Z-P.description: Major outage, PR crisis, key personnel loss
D-2-Z-P.reason: Crisis moments, Contradiction Analysis finds primary/secondary, Seek Truth forces facing truth, Redundancy Backup is last defense.
steps:
Step 1: Classify severity (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> Is this P0 (fatal), P1 (severe), P2 (general)?
  -> What is principal contradiction? Secondary?
  -> Who is decision maker? Executor? Informed?

Step 2: Stop bleeding (Seek Truth)
  -> Admit problem, no cover-up, no blame-shifting
  -> Take most direct stop-loss action
  -> E.g., outage->cut traffic/degrade/rollback; PR->apologize/publish facts/rectify

Step 3: Activate backup (Redundancy Backup)
  -> Critical paths have Plan B?
  -> Key person has backup?
  -> Data/service has geo-redundancy?

Step 4: Root cause retrospective
  -> 5 whys, dig to systemic root cause
  -> Distinguish: technical, process, management, culture causes
  -> Create action items: owner, deadline, acceptance criteria

Step 5: Institutionalize
  -> Turn lessons into norms/tools/processes
  -> Drill: regular fault drills/crisis simulations
  -> Retro: next time same issue caught and stopped in minutes?
expected: P0 outage recovery <30 minutes
PR crisis 24hr turnaround
Same issue zero recurrence
D-2-Z-P.case:
An e-commerce big promo core transaction chain outage 15 min.
Contradiction: Principal contradiction is DB master write block, secondary is cache penetration.
Seek Truth: Admit outage, cut read-only mode stop loss, public apology.
Redundancy: Replica promoted to master, geo-backup restored data.
Root cause: Promo pre-heat script unrate-limited caused write storm.
Institutionalize: Pre-promo mandatory stress test, rate limit, circuit breaker trio.
Result: Next year promo zero outage, fault drill routine established.

D-3-Z-P.name: Survival Crisis
D-3-Z-P.description: Company near bankruptcy, project about to be cut, personal job loss/major illness
D-3-Z-P.reason: Survival moments tolerate zero fakes and delays. Seek Truth forces facing brutal reality, Contradiction Analysis finds the one lifeline in chaos, Redundancy Backup is last lifeline - critical paths must have alternatives.
steps:
Step 1: Face reality (Seek Truth)
  -> Stop all sugarcoating, delays, wishful thinking
  -> Write: how many months cash runway? core business survival?
  -> List all debts, commitments, hard costs

Step 2: Find the one lifeline (Contradiction Analysis)
  -> List all problems, find only the if-unsolved-tomorrow-we-die one
  -> Everything else paused, all hands on this one
  -> E.g., cash flow break is principal contradiction, strategy/culture/brand all yield

Step 3: Configure redundancy (Redundancy Backup)
  -> Critical paths must have Plan B, Plan C
  -> Cash: min 3 months operating reserve
  -> Key talent: critical roles must have backups
  -> Core business: must have degradation mode (e.g., manual/read-only fallback)

Step 4: Extreme focus execution
  -> Everyone only does survival-relevant work
  -> Daily standup: what did for survival yesterday? what today?
  -> Cut all non-cash-generating/non-life-saving projects/meetings/reports

Step 5: Find turning point
  -> Parallel: fundraising/monetization/M&A/pivot
  -> Daily eval: which path has highest survival probability?
  -> Concentrate resources on highest-probability path
expected: Cash flow positive or funded in 30 days
Core business uninterrupted
Core team zero attrition
D-3-Z-P.case:
Startup funding failed, 3 months payroll left.
Seek Truth: Admit no-funding=death, stop all new feature dev.
Contradiction: Core is cash flow, rest is noise.
Redundancy: Core engineers have backup, key services have fallback.
Extreme focus: All pivot to quick-revenue custom delivery.
Freeze hiring, cut office costs, founders no salary.
Result: Big deal day 45, cash flow positive day 60, bridge funding day 90.

B-1-Y-S.name: Innovation Breakthrough
B-1-Y-S.description: Tech innovation, business model innovation, disruptive innovation
B-1-Y-S.reason: Innovation is not linear, but mutation. Natural Selection reminds: many trials, fast iterations, keep what fits. Punctuated Equilibrium tells: breakthroughs often from paradigm shifts. Flexible Strategy lets you not dead-end on single path.
steps:
Step 1: Multi-path exploration (Natural Selection)
  -> Simultaneously try 3-5 different tech/business paths
  -> Each path small resource, clear stop-loss
  -> Don't put all eggs in one basket

Step 2: Spot paradigm shift (Punctuated Equilibrium)
  -> Watch: any new theory, tool, infrastructure emerging?
  -> Ask: can this change make previously "impossible" become "possible"?
  -> e.g., Transformer made NLP from RNN obsolete

Step 3: Rapid validation and screening (Flexible Strategy)
  -> Each path does minimum viability validation (MVP/prototype/experiment)
  -> Data speaks, not intuition
  -> Stop-loss: underperforming paths decisively cut

Step 4: Focused breakthrough
  -> Resources concentrate on most promising 1 path
  -> Concentrate firepower on core challenge
  -> Build tech/commercial moat

Step 5: Scale up
  -> On validated basis, rapid expansion
  -> Standardize, automate, platformize
  -> Form new growth curve
expected: Avoid 6+ months wasted on wrong direction
Establish multi-path exploration mechanism
Breakthrough speed 2-3x
B-1-Y-S.case:
A company wants to do AI drug discovery.
Natural Selection: Simultaneously explore molecule generation, protein folding, virtual screening 3 paths.
Punctuated Equilibrium: AlphaFold2 released, protein folding solved (paradigm shift).
Flexible Strategy: Decisively cut protein folding self-dev, leverage AlphaFold2 for downstream apps.
Focus breakthrough: Concentrate resources on molecule generation challenge.
Result: 6 months launched first candidate drug, entered pre-clinical.

C-1-Y-P.name: Team Building
C-1-Y-P.description: Forming new team, team integration, culture shaping
C-1-Y-P.reason: Team isn't ready just by hiring. Mass Line ensures hearing real voices, United Front helps integrate differences, Management by Objectives aligns everyone to goals.
steps:
Step 1: Deep understanding (Mass Line)
  -> 1-on-1 deep interviews each member
  -> Ask: what you excel at? want to do? worry about?
  -> Log: skill matrix, willingness matrix, concerns list

Step 2: Find consensus (United Front)
  -> Identify core values overlap
  -> Find "greatest common divisor" as team culture foundation
  -> Allow differences, but core must align

Step 3: Set goals (Management by Objectives)
  -> Jointly create OKRs, not top-down decomposition
  -> Goals challenging but achievable
  -> Establish weekly/monthly/quarterly review rhythm

Step 4: Establish mechanisms
  -> Weekly: sync progress, expose problems, mutual help
  -> Retro: victory retro, failure retro, all retro
  -> Feedback: timely, specific, actionable

Step 5: Continuous iteration
  -> Quarterly review: culture healthy? goals aligned?
  -> Adjust: people, process, incentives
  -> New member onboarding: culture package
expected: Team cohesion significantly improved
Goal alignment >90%
Per capita output up 30%+
C-1-Y-P.case:
A startup core team expanded from 5 to 20.
Mass Line: Founder 1-on-1 each, found "tech debt" biggest pain.
United Front: Established "User value first, Tech excellence, Radical transparency" three values.
MBO: All participate in quarterly OKRs, weekly public progress.
Result: 6 months delivered 3 core versions, zero major incidents, team satisfaction 4.8/5.

steps: 改革北京大学，引入学术自由与民主治校理念
实行'五育并举'，将体育、智育、德育、审美、公民教育体系化
推行'以美育代宗教'，建立全新的精神启蒙信仰框架
推动学科体系标准化，接轨国际一流标准
通过人才培养体系革新，实现教育救国目标
expected: 学术独立与大学治理体系转型
美育代宗教的精神启蒙范式
高等教育科学治校体系建设
P5-EDU-002.case: 担任北京大学校长，推行'思想自由，兼容并包'；推行'五育并举'教育体系；创办国立艺术专科学校；教育救国思想的体系实践

P5-EDU-003.name: 梁漱溟：乡村建设与文化伦理的信仰重构
P5-EDU-003.description: 乡村建设、东方文化、伦理学
P5-EDU-003.reason: 梁漱溟视乡村建设为民族文化复兴的信仰工程，通过复兴儒家伦理，在乡村基层重构中国社会的文化认同与自治能力。
steps: 在山东邹平开展乡村建设实验，探索中国式现代化道路
批判西方个人主义与个人物质追求的误区
构建以伦理为基础的乡村治理体系
提倡东西方文化互补，在现代文明中融入中国传统智慧
建立基层教育网络，重构平民信仰与组织形式
expected: 中国式乡村自治建设范式
东方文化现代伦理实践
社会文化认同的基石构建
P5-EDU-003.case: 山东邹平乡村建设实验；著作《中国文化要义》；伦理建设与基层教育的体系实践；东西方文化比较与启蒙

P5-EDU-004.name: 马相伯：独立学术与教育救国的信仰奠基
P5-EDU-004.description: 震旦学院、教育救国、学术独立
P5-EDU-004.reason: 马相伯以'教育救国'为终身信仰，坚持教育独立于外力控制，通过创办震旦学院实现高等教育的本土化与自主性。
steps: 创办震旦学院，坚持学术独立于外方控制
推行高等教育自主化，强调学生素质与社会责任
积极倡导教育救国，建立多层次的平民教育启蒙网络
利用学术影响力推动教育标准与国际化进程
在关键历史时期持续呼吁爱国教育
expected: 高等教育自主化范式
教育救国人才体系
独立学术机构建设
P5-EDU-004.case: 创办震旦学院；复旦公学创办的关键参与；长期的教育救国奔走；独立教育实践与抗战救国活动

P5-EDU-005.name: 晏阳初：平民教育与乡村建设的信仰赋能
P5-EDU-005.description: 平民教育、乡村建设、识字运动
P5-EDU-005.reason: 晏阳初视平民教育为乡村发展的信仰之基，推行四大教育体系（文、生、卫、公），通过赋能平民增强乡村自治实力。
steps: 推行平民识字运动，打破阶层文化鸿沟
建立乡村建设实验区，通过四大教育模式赋能农民
采取实验主义策略，先试点、后推广，逐步完善乡村体系
重视农民的主体作用，强调由下而上的社会变革
推动国际合作，将平民教育范式推广至发展中国家
expected: 乡村平民赋能体系
实验主义教育推广范式
乡村建设治理实效
P5-EDU-005.case: 推行平民识字运动；建立定县乡村建设实验区；四大教育体系：文（识字）、生（农业）、卫（健康）、公（自治）；平民教育国际化实践

P5-EDU-006.name: 杨昌济：人格教育与道德修养的信仰塑造
P5-EDU-006.description: 人格教育、道德修养、青年启蒙
P5-EDU-006.reason: 杨昌济以人格教育为信仰核心，通过修身与道德启蒙，旨在塑造具有独立人格和爱国情怀的青年领袖，影响深远。
steps: 在湖南第一师范推行修身教育，强化学生品格磨砺
强调'致良知'与'知行合一'，消除认知与行动的差距
推行坦诚的批评与自我批评，通过反思实现个人成长
注重人格教育，将青年启蒙与国家民族存亡联系起来
在学术中融入道德要求，培育具备科学眼光与报国情怀的人才
expected: 青年人格教育与道德启蒙范式
知行合一的教育实践闭环
高素质人才培养的品格奠基
P5-EDU-006.case: 在湖南第一师范任教；教导毛泽东、蔡和森等；《达化斋日记》与道德教育实践；人格修养与青年启蒙范式

P5-EDU-007.name: 晏阳初：平民教育与识字运动的社会教育学
P5-EDU-007.description: 四大教育、三大力、识字运动
P5-EDU-007.reason: 晏阳初通过识字运动普及基础教育，以“平民教育”作为信仰，重塑了乡村民众的知识结构与社会参与意志。
steps: 识别民众教育痛点，发起声势浩大的识字运动
提出四大教育（文、生、卫、公民）体系，全方位重塑平民知识结构
将平民受教育权作为信仰确立，激发社会自我提升意志
通过平民学校将行为规范向乡村普及
建立民众自我参与的社会教育管理范式
expected: 平民识字与启蒙教育体系
民众社会参与的制度化路径
农村基础教育与社会重塑范式
P5-EDU-007.case: 晏阳初创办平民教育促进会；定县乡村实验；发起平民识字运动；编纂平民教材

P5-EDU-008.name: 吴玉章：革命教育与老年教育的终身实践
P5-EDU-008.description: 延安教育、文字改革、终身学习
P5-EDU-008.reason: 吴玉章将教育视为革命生命力，通过延安的革命教育与晚年的文字改革，展示了以终身学习作为信仰重塑意志的卓越实践。
steps: 在延安建立适应革命需求的革命教育体系
将教育作为激发群众革命觉悟与意志的行为规范
推动汉字简化与文字改革，促进全民受教育权
以终身学习作为晚年信仰，重塑其群体影响力
建立适应不同阶段的革命人才培养范式
expected: 革命时期教育建设范式
全民文字与基础教育改革机制
以教育引领社会意志的实践范式
P5-EDU-008.case: 吴玉章担任中国人民大学校长；主持汉字简化方案；在延安负责革命教育工作

P5-ETH-Apai.name: 阿沛·阿旺晋美
P5-ETH-Apai.description: 阿沛·阿旺晋美作为西藏和平解放的代表，是实施民族区域自治的关键人物，通过参与制定《民族区域自治法》，成功将民族自主权与国家统一法律框架融合，是民族共治模式的典型践行者。

P5-ETH-WangEnmao.name: 王恩茂
P5-ETH-WangEnmao.description: 王恩茂长期主持新疆工作，通过推动生产建设兵团参与地方建设，实现了边疆边防力量与民族地方自治的融合，确保了边疆地区的稳固与发展。

P5-ETH-Ulanhu.name: 乌兰夫
P5-ETH-Ulanhu.description: 乌兰夫成功创建了第一个少数民族自治政权，在处理多民族聚居地区的民族团结与政权建设中，确立了民族区域自治的范例。

P5-ETH-Saifuding.name: 赛福鼎·艾则孜
P5-ETH-Saifuding.description: 赛福鼎作为维吾尔族第一位共产党员，通过参与“三区革命”到新疆和平解放的整个过程，是民族区域自治政策在边疆少数民族地区贯彻执行的核心领导者。

P5-SCI-001.name: 李四光
P5-SCI-001.description: 李四光（1889-1971），中国地质力学的创立者，中国现代地质学的奠基人之一。他提出了一系列具有创新性的地质理论，为中国能源、资源开发及国家工业化建设做出了杰出贡献。

P5-SCI-002.name: 竺可桢
P5-SCI-002.description: 竺可桢（1890-1974），中国近代地理学与气象学的奠基人，中国物候学的创始人，长期从事气象事业的组织与气象教育事业。

P5-SCI-003.name: 赵忠尧
P5-SCI-003.description: 赵忠尧（1902-1998），著名核物理学家，中国原子核物理、中子物理、加速器研究的先驱和启蒙者，被称为“大师们的老师”。

P5-SCI-004.name: 叶企孙
P5-SCI-004.description: 叶企孙（1898-1977），著名物理学家、教育家，中国物理学界的一代宗师，为中国现代物理学及科技人才的培养做出了奠基性贡献。

P5-SCI-005.name: 谈家桢
P5-SCI-005.description: 谈家桢（1909-2008），著名国际遗传学家，中国现代遗传学的奠基人，推动中国生命科学教育与研究迈向国际领先地位。

P5-SCI-006.name: 郭永怀
P5-SCI-006.description: 郭永怀（1909-1968），中国现代力学事业的奠基人之一，唯一以烈士身份被授予“两弹一星”功勋奖章的科学家。

SE-INN-001.name_en: Nobel/Krumbach-Ericsson: Invention-Industry-Telecom Triple Helix Innovation Ecosystem
SE-INN-001.description_en: Swedish innovation ecosystem via triple helix across century: Alfred Nobel (1833-1896) invented dynamite/detonator, built patent-capital-brand trinity, will established Nobel Prizes elevating "invention" to "human welfare" global standard; Karin Krumbach (1920-2011) with husband built Atlas Copco, turned compressed air tech into global mining/construction standard equipment, embodying "invention→industry" conversion; Lars Magnus Ericsson (1900-1989) founded Ericsson, from telephone manufacturing to global telecom infrastructure empire, achieving "industry→infrastructure" leap. All three exemplify M158 Polymath Integration—full-spectrum innovation across physics/chemistry/mechanical/electrical/commerce/standardization. Core mechanism: patent protection → capital reinvestment → global standard setting → talent magnet → next invention cycle.
SE-INN-001.reason_en: Sweden without natural resources builds innovation nation via "invention-patent-capital-standard" closed loop. Three generations across chemistry/mechanical/electrical show M158 Polymath Integration & M151 Trust Capital exponential compounding in business ecosystems.
steps_en: Invention patented & capitalized: Nobel 355 patents, dynamite monopoly → global military/mining supply chain, wealth anchored Nobel Foundation
Industry standardized & platformed: Ericsson AXE digital switch global standard, GSM/3G/4G/5G standard-setting leadership
Talent magnet & knowledge spillover: KTH/Uppsala/Lund three engineering powerhouses, Stockholm unicorn density global #2
Trust capital institutionalized: Stockholm Stock Exchange transparency, PRV efficiency, tripartite model extended to innovation policy
Global public goods output: Nobel Prize = science's highest honor; Ericsson 5G patent pool licensing; Atlas Copco sustainable productivity
SE-INN-001.expected_en: Small nation via "invention-patent-capital-standard" quaternity closed loop achieves high-value manufacturing & global rule-setting dual win, innovation index consistently global top 3.
SE-INN-001.case_en: Sweden 2023 GII #2; Ericsson 5G SEP declarations global top 3; Stockholm unicorns per capita #2 after Silicon Valley; Nobel Prize 120+ years zero-controversy authority.
SE-INN-001.cross_cultural_impact: Nobel Prize global science governance; Ericsson telecom standards; Swedish triple helix model for innovation policy
SE-INN-001.spiritual_tradition: Lutheran stewardship + Wallenberg family industrial ethics
SE-INN-001.colonial_history: No colonies; Swedish East India Company 18th century trade only
SE-INN-001.diaspora_influence: Swedish-American 4M+ in US Midwest, shaped Minnesota politics/industry

ZA-MAN-001.reason_en: Mandela represents how reconciliation politics transcends retribution cycles through moral authority, demonstrating how truth commissions achieve healing in post-conflict societies, his Rainbow Nation vision becoming global transitional justice paradigm benchmark.
steps_en: Study Mandela early ANC Youth League and armed struggle turn
Analyze 1964 Rivonia Trial I am prepared to die speech
Explore 27 years prison reading/negotiation/reconciliation roadmap prep
Evaluate 1994 election and TRC Tutu chaired hearings
Summarize anti-apartheid truth reconciliation rainbow morality paradigm contribution for global transitional justice
ZA-MAN-001.expected_en: Master how moral authority transforms into political reconciliation institutional design, understand truth commission hearing mechanism balancing justice and healing, evaluate Mandela model direct lessons for Rwanda Sierra Leone truth commissions.
ZA-MAN-001.case_en: 1994 elected; 1995 TRC; Rainbow Nation; 2013 death. Anti-apartheid truth reconciliation rainbow morality paradigm endures.
ZA-MAN-001.cross_cultural_impact: Truth commission; forgiveness; Rainbow Nation; transitional justice; moral authority

NO-PEACE-001.description_en: Fridtjof Nansen (1861-1930), Norwegian explorer, scientist, diplomat, first League of Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, invented "Nansen passport" saving hundreds of thousands of stateless refugees; Gro Harlem Brundtland (1939-), Norway's first female PM, WHO Director-General, drove the Brundtland Commission's "Our Common Future" report. Across eras, both embody Nordic peace diplomacy: small nations leveraging moral authority and institutional innovation to carve survival space among great powers.
NO-PEACE-001.reason_en: Nansen established the "small nation as moral great power" diplomatic paradigm; Brundtland extended it into global sustainable development governance. Their cross-generational relay perfectly exemplifies the compounding effect of Nordic Trust Capital (M151) and Ubuntu-style consensus (M146) in international institution-building.
steps_en: Establish moral authority: ground legitimacy beyond geopolitics in scientific/humanitarian achievement
Invent institutional tools: create replicable international public goods like Nansen passport/sustainable development framework
Mobilize transnational coalitions: organize scientists, NGOs, IOs across borders for collective action
Lock in long-term mechanisms: convert ad hoc humanitarian action into permanent international law/governance architecture
Intergenerational transmission & compounding: Brundtland relayed Nansen, upgrading peace diplomacy to planetary governance
NO-PEACE-001.expected_en: In great power interstices, small nations gain strategic autonomy via moral authority + institutional innovation; establish replicable international public goods supply model, achieving intergenerational trust capital compounding.
NO-PEACE-001.case_en: 1922 Nansen passport gave 400k Russian/Armenian refugees legal identity; 1987 Brundtland Report made "sustainable development" global consensus, directly birthing 1992 Rio Summit & Paris Agreement framework.
NO-PEACE-001.cross_cultural_impact: Nansen passport precedent for modern refugee law; Brundtland Commission defined sustainable development globally
NO-PEACE-001.colonial_history: Norway independent 1905; no colonial empire but whaling/Arctic presence
NO-PEACE-001.diaspora_influence: Norwegian-American community shaped US Midwest politics
NO-PEACE-001.indigenous_knowledge_system: Sami traditional knowledge recognized in later Nordic governance (not directly in these figures)

NO-ENER-001.name_en: Statoil/Equinor: North Sea Oil & Sovereign Wealth Governance
NO-ENER-001.description_en: Norway's state oil company (Statoil, founded 1972, renamed Equinor 2018) led North Sea development; profits flow directly into the Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG), now >$1.5T, world's largest SWF. Core governance: 100% resource rent to state, Ethics Council excludes unethical investments, cross-party consensus locks "spend only returns not principal". This exemplifies Nordic Trust Capital (M151) institutionalized for resource curse mitigation (M168) with intergenerational compounding.
NO-ENER-001.reason_en: Norway avoided Dutch disease & resource curse by turning geological luck into institutional dividends: transparency + ethical constraints + intergenerational contract. Equinor's pivot from oil to offshore wind/CCS/hydrogen demonstrates M169 post-resource transition governance.
steps_en: Resource sovereignty: 1963 Continental Shelf Act established state ownership of seabed resources
Create NOC: Statoil 100% state-owned, technical autonomy + profit upstreaming
Legislate revenue lock-in: 1990 Pension Fund Act, spend only 3% real return
Ethical oversight: independent council can exclude tobacco/weapons/severe ESG violators
Transition anchored in long-termism: 2020 climate roadmap, net-zero 2050, 12-16GW offshore wind target
NO-ENER-001.expected_en: Resource-rich small nation achieves intergenerational wealth preservation/growth, avoids Dutch disease, establishes replicable gold standard for resource governance.
NO-ENER-001.case_en: GPFG 2023 value NOK 15.6T, ~NOK 2.9M per capita; Equinor 2023 renewables >30% capex, Dogger Bank world's largest wind farm.
NO-ENER-001.cross_cultural_impact: Global SWF governance model; Santiago Principles co-author; resource curse avoidance case study worldwide
NO-ENER-001.colonial_history: Norway independent 1905; no colonies but Arctic whaling history
NO-ENER-001.resource_curse_mitigation: 100% resource rent to SWF; 3% spending rule; Ethics Council exclusion list; full transparency (EITI founding member)

DK-FLEX-001.description_en: Denmark's "flexicurity" model built by three cross-party leaders over 30 years: Poul Schlüter (Conservative, 1982-93) drove labor reforms; Poul Nyrup Rasmussen (Social Dem, 1993-2001) institutionalized four pillars (flexible firing + generous unemployment + active labor policy + lifelong learning); Helle Thorning-Schmidt (Social Dem, 2011-15) added digital public services & green transition. Core logic: firms get firing flexibility, workers get income security & retraining rights, state bears adjustment costs. This exemplifies Nordic Trust Capital (M151) institutionalized—high trust lowers transaction costs so "flexibility" doesn't become "insecurity".
DK-FLEX-001.reason_en: Flexicurity is Nordic model's self-evolution under globalization: institutionalized trust replaces rigid protection, achieving dynamic balance of firm competitiveness & worker security. Three leaders' cross-party relay shows compounding of M34 Institutionalization & M52 Long-termism.
steps_en: Consensus building: Employer confederation + union confederation + government tripartite lock core principles
Legislative anchoring: 1994/1998/2002 three reform acts writing four pillars into law
Institutionalize ALMP: municipal job centers, mandatory activation, skills upgrade accounts
Lifelong learning finance: adult education subsidies, vocational college network, corporate training tax credits
Digital & green extension: NemID/digital post universal, 2030 Climate Act locks 70% emissions cut
DK-FLEX-001.expected_en: Unemployment consistently below EU average, high labor participation, firm innovation index leading, welfare state sustainable in open economy.
DK-FLEX-001.case_en: 2008 GFC Denmark unemployment peak 6.2% (EU 10%+), recovered in 2 years; COVID wage subsidy live in 2 weeks, saved 90% jobs.
DK-FLEX-001.cross_cultural_impact: EU flexicurity principles 2007; ILO model; OECD benchmark for labor market resilience
DK-FLEX-001.spiritual_tradition: Lutheran work ethic + Grundtvigian folk high school tradition
DK-FLEX-001.colonial_history: Greenland/Faroe Islands autonomous; historical Caribbean/India trade posts
DK-FLEX-001.diaspora_influence: Danish-American community in US Midwest; shipping diaspora global
DK-FLEX-001.indigenous_knowledge_system: Inuit traditional knowledge in Greenland self-governance (indirect)

DK-DES-001.name_en: Paul Henningsen/LEGO/Børge Olsen: Design Engineering Commercialization & Systemic Innovation
DK-DES-001.description_en: Danish design engineering tradition across three generations: Poul Henningsen (1894-1967) established PH lamp system—"function determines form, optics scientized"; LEGO Group (founded 1932, Godtfred Christiansen 1958 brick patent) took modular standardization to extreme, building "toy as platform" ecosystem; Børge Olsen (1928-2018) with system furniture (1960s) drove industrialized housing/office standardization. All three exemplify M158 Polymath Integration—holographic prototype validation across optics/materials/manufacturing/commerce/human-factors. Core mechanism: modular standard → platform ecosystem → user co-creation → brand moat.
DK-DES-001.reason_en: Danish design is not mere aesthetics but "engineered aesthetics": scientific principles (optics/ergonomics) → modular standards → industrial manufacturing → commercial platform. Three generations century-long relay shows M158 Polymath Integration & M151 Trust Capital compounding in business ecosystems.
steps_en: Scientific principles first: Henningsen used logarithmic spiral for shade curvature, eliminating glare (pure physics)
Modular standard definition: LEGO brick 1958 patent tolerance 0.002mm, backward compatible 60+ years
Platform ecosystem building: LEGO Ideas/Technic/Education make users co-creators, IP licensing two-way
System furniture industrialization: Olsen modular storage/office systems fitted Danish welfare state public procurement
Brand moat deepening: Design museum acquisitions + IP protection + premium pricing + education permeation = cultural barrier
DK-DES-001.expected_en: Small nation without natural resources builds global brand moat via "design engineering" core competency, achieving high-value manufacturing & cultural export win-win.
DK-DES-001.case_en: LEGO 2023 revenue DKK 65.9B, brand value global top 10; PH lamps permanent MoMA/Centre Pompidou; Olsen systems in airports/universities/governments worldwide.
DK-DES-001.cross_cultural_impact: Global design education curriculum; modular platform business model; Scandinavian design brand equity
DK-DES-001.spiritual_tradition: Lutheran craft ethics + Grundtvigian democratic design
DK-DES-001.colonial_history: No direct colonial design legacy; Greenlandic craft influence contemporary
DK-DES-001.diaspora_influence: Danish designers shaped US mid-century modern (Eames collaboration)
DK-DES-001.indigenous_knowledge_system: Inuit material culture influences contemporary Arctic design (indirect)

FI-SISU-001.name_en: Sininheimo/Linus Torvalds: Sisu Resilience & Open Source Governance
FI-SISU-001.description_en: Finnish "Sisu"—calm grit in extreme adversity, action-oriented, execution without complaint—transmitted across eras: Paavo Sininheimo (1888-1972), Winter/Continuation War commander, held Mannerheim Line against overwhelming odds, military Sisu; Linus Torvalds (1969-), created Linux kernel, governs world's largest collaborative software project (28M LOC, 20k+ contributors) with "talk less, code more" violent aesthetics, technical Sisu. Core mechanism: minimal rules (kernel mailing list + maintainer trust chain) + absolute technical authority + refusal of bureaucratization. This exemplifies M151 Nordic Trust Capital realized at code layer—trust via code quality not contracts.
FI-SISU-001.reason_en: Sisu isn't blind persistence but "rational action in despair". Sininheimo calculated ballistics precisely amid shortages; Torvalds established strict merge standards amid chaotic contributions. Cross military/tech domains, showing deep isomorphism of M35 Foolish Old Man Moves Mountains & M51 Autonomous R&D.
steps_en: Acknowledge hard limits: Winter War USSR 4:1 superiority / open source chaos, no denial no fantasy
Focus on controllable variables: line geometry/ammo allocation / merge standards/maintainer hierarchy, minimal rules
Violent aesthetics execution: "no merging garbage code" / "retreat = planned enemy delay", zero tolerance compromise
Trust chain building: maintainer tree delegation / officer corps graded command, trust via delivery not title
Intergenerational transmission & openness: Linux Foundation neutral stewardship / Finnish Defence University strategic teaching, Sisu becomes transmissible asset
FI-SISU-001.expected_en: Small nation in great power squeeze/tech monopoly builds asymmetric survival advantage via "minimal rules + absolute technical authority + cultural resilience", outputting global public goods (Linux/defense strategy).
FI-SISU-001.case_en: Linux runs 90%+ world servers/supercomputers/Android; Finland 1939-44 two wars kept independence, Cold War "Finlandization" became neutral survival paradigm.
FI-SISU-001.intellectual_tradition: Finnish Sisu / Hacker Culture / Open Source Governance
FI-SISU-001.cross_cultural_impact: Linux governance model for decentralized collaboration; Sisu concept adopted in global resilience literature
FI-SISU-001.diaspora_influence: Finnish-American in Minnesota/Upper Peninsula mining communities
FI-SISU-001.indigenous_knowledge_system: Sami traditional knowledge recognized in Finnish law (limited)

SA-WAH-001.name_en: Ibn Saud/Abdulaziz: Wahhabi Islamic Governance & State-Building
SA-WAH-001.description_en: Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud (1875-1953) aka Ibn Saud, with Wahhabi doctrine as ideological core, from Najd base -> recaptured Riyadh (1902) -> conquered Al-Hasa (1913) -> unified Hejaz (1925) -> established Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (1932). Core governance mechanism: Wahhabi fiqh (Hanbali strict literalism) as state law, Ulama (religious scholars) check royal power via Shura (consultation), tribal alliance (Ikhwan) as military mobilization base, oil revenue (discovered 1938) distribution establishing social contract. Exemplifies M161 Waqf-style Islamic Modern Philanthropic Governance—religious endowments perpetual, proceeds earmarked, community self-governance—and M168 Oil/Mineral Geostrategy.
SA-WAH-001.reason_en: Saudi state-building not mere military conquest but trinity of "doctrine+tribe+fiqh": Wahhabi doctrine provides legitimacy, Ikhwan provides military force, fiqh provides governance framework. M161+M168 combined, distinct from M149 Islamic Shura (decision-making) and M173 Hashemite Legitimacy (lineage), core: "fiqh as constitution, tribe as army, oil as social contract".
steps_en: Doctrinal legitimacy establishment: 1744 Saudi-Wahhabi pact, doctrine as political platform
Tribal military mobilization: Ikhwan settlements sedentarize nomads, religious zeal converts to conquest drive
Fiqh governance institutionalization: Ulama council reviews legislation, judiciary independent from admin, Hanafi/Hanbali coexistence
Oil social contract anchoring: 1938 Dammam No.1 -> Aramco JV -> revenue distribution/tax-free/welfare state
Modernization transition management: Fahd (1975-82) infra/education/industrialization, Abdullah (2005-15) women rights/judicial reform/MBS Vision 2030
SA-WAH-001.expected_en: Tribal alliance builds modern state via "fiqh as constitution, oil as contract" mechanism, achieving regime continuity & strategic autonomy amid traditional doctrine & modernization pressures.
SA-WAH-001.case_en: 1902 Riyadh recaptured -> 1932 state founded -> 1938 oil discovered -> 1973 oil embargo establishes energy superpower status -> 2016 Vision 2030 launches post-oil transition, 90 years zero regime change.
SA-WAH-001.cross_cultural_impact: Wahhabi model for Islamic governance; OPEC founding; petrodollar recycling; Vision 2030 reform benchmark
SA-WAH-001.colonial_history: Ottoman suzerainty nominal; British protectorate relations 1915-1927
SA-WAH-001.resource_curse_mitigation: Aramco 50/50 profit sharing (1950) -> full nationalization (1980); SAMA sovereign wealth management; Vision 2030 diversification

SA-OIL-001.name_en: Ahmed Zaki Yamani/Oil Ministers: Oil Geostrategy & OPEC Power Architecture
SA-OIL-001.description_en: Ahmed Zaki Yamani (1930-2021) served as Saudi Oil Minister 1962-1986, OPEC chief architect. Core strategy: 1973 oil embargo as geopolitical weapon, establishing "oil for security" US-Saudi alliance framework; drove OPEC from price-taker to price-setter, establishing production quotas/official selling prices/revenue allocation mechanisms; advocated "fair price" balancing producer-consumer interests, avoiding accelerated Western alternative energy R&D. Exemplifies M168 Oil Geostrategy—resource sovereign states reshaping global energy order via collective monopoly—and M169 Post-Oil Transition foresight (Yamani early invested in downstream refining/petrochemicals/renewables).
SA-OIL-001.reason_en: Yamani not mere technocrat but "oil diplomacy master": leveraging resource monopoly to restructure geopolitics. M168 distinct from M39 Birdcage Economy (general) and M169 Post-Resource Transition (post-oil), core: "oil as diplomatic currency, OPEC as geopolitical alliance, price as strategic tool".
steps_en: OPEC institutionalization: 1960 Baghdad founding -> 1970s quotas/official prices/revenue allocation three pillars established
1973 embargo geopolitical lever: Arab producers cut/embargo West, oil price 4x, Western economic shock
"Oil for security" framework: US military protects Saudi/Gulf security, Saudi maintains capacity/dollar pricing/Treasury recycling
Downstream value chain extension: invest in refineries/petrochemicals/shipping/renewables, capture full value chain
Talent & standards export: KFUPM/Aramco training/technical standards Arabization, regional talent magnet
SA-OIL-001.expected_en: Resource sovereign states achieve strategic autonomy & intergenerational wealth from geological endowment via trinity of "monopoly pricing + geopolitical leverage + value chain extension", reshaping global energy governance rules.
SA-OIL-001.case_en: 1973 oil crisis price $3->$12/bbl; OPEC market share peak 55%; Yamani led 24 years until 1986 dismissal; Aramco fully nationalized 1980.
SA-OIL-001.cross_cultural_impact: OPEC model for commodity cartels; petrodollar recycling; energy security doctrine
SA-OIL-001.colonial_history: Ottoman/British influence; Aramco US consortium origin
SA-OIL-001.resource_curse_mitigation: OPEC quota discipline; downstream diversification; Yamani personal renewables investment

SA-VIS-001.name_en: Mohammed bin Salman/Vision 2030: Post-Oil Transition Governance & Tech Sovereignty
SA-VIS-001.description_en: Mohammed bin Salman (1985-) Crown Prince 2015, launched Vision 2030 2016: three pillars—vibrant society (tourism/culture/entertainment/sports), thriving economy (PIF SWF $7T+, NEOM/Red Sea/Jeddah new cities, green hydrogen/semiconductors/biotech), ambitious government (digitalization/transparency/female labor participation 30%+). Core tensions: authoritarian modernization vs social conservatism, foreign capital dependency vs tech sovereignty, regional hegemony vs international isolation risk (Khashoggi/Yemen war). Exemplifies M169 Post-Oil Transition Governance—SWF reinvestment anchoring knowledge economy, and M158 Polymath Integration—full-spectrum national transformation engineering across energy/tech/finance/urban planning/social engineering.
SA-VIS-001.reason_en: MBS attempts single-generation leap from 'oil rentier state to knowledge economy powerhouse', M169's extreme stress test: PIF as national VC, NEOM as greenfield lab, social opening as talent magnet. Distinct from M168 (mitigation) and M170 (stability), core: 'single-generational leapfrog transition + SWF as national venture capital + greenfield new city experiment'.
steps_en: PIF as national VC: assets from $150B to $7T+, investing in Uber/SoftBank/Lucid/gaming/green hydrogen
NEOM greenfield lab: $500B zero-carbon city, The Line linear city/hydrogen export/biotech/tourism
Social contract rewrite: women driving/entertainment opening/labor law reform/anti-corruption (Ritz-Carlton) reshaping elite pact
Digital government & transparency: Absher app services/open data/procurement transparency/KPI performance mgmt
Regional diplomacy restructuring: Gulf reconciliation/Israel normalization exploration/Yemen ceasefire/Red Sea security alliance
SA-VIS-001.expected_en: Single-generational post-oil transition achieving 'oil rent->SWF->knowledge economy->tech sovereignty' closed loop, success or failure provides extreme case for resource states.
SA-VIS-001.case_en: PIF 2023 assets $700B+; NEOM 2024 construction started; female labor participation 2017 20%->2023 35%; non-oil revenue 2016 38%->2023 50%+; but Yemen war/Khashoggi/human rights controversies persist.
SA-VIS-001.cross_cultural_impact: Vision 2030 benchmark for Gulf diversification; NEOM urban experiment; PIF global investment model
SA-VIS-001.colonial_history: No direct colonial rule; British treaty relations 1915-1927
SA-VIS-001.resource_curse_mitigation: PIF diversification; NEOM green hydrogen; non-oil revenue target 50% by 2030; ESG reporting

IQ-CAL-001.name_en: Caliph al-Mansur/Baghdad Caliphs: Islamic Legal Caliphate Governance & Imperial Order
IQ-CAL-001.description_en: Abu Ja'far Abdullah al-Mansur (714-775), 2nd Abbasid Caliph, built Round City of Baghdad (762), established proto-separation of powers 'Caliph-Vizier-Diwan': Caliph holds supreme religious/military authority, Vizier (chief minister) heads administration, Diwan (departments) divide jurisdiction. Core governance tech: Islamic law (Fiqh) legislative/judicial unification, Bayt al-Mal (treasury) fiscal centralization, four Sunni madhhabs (Maliki/Hanafi/Shafi'i/Hanbali) coexist & compete, Bay'ah (oath of allegiance) as political legitimacy. Exemplifies M160 Islamic Legal/Caliphal Governance—divine law as constitution, scholar class as bureaucracy, oath of allegiance as political contract.
IQ-CAL-001.reason_en: Abbasid Caliphate not theocratic autocracy but trinity of 'fiqh constitution + scholar bureaucracy + allegiance contract': Caliph bound by fiqh, Qadis independent adjudication, Ulama check caliphal power. M160 distinct from M149 Islamic Shura (consultative decision) and M161 Waqf Philanthropy (asset perpetuity), core: 'fiqh as constitution, scholars as bureaucracy, allegiance as contract' imperial-grade governance OS.
steps_en: Round city planning & symbolic power: 762 Round Baghdad, geometric order mirroring cosmic/fiqh order
Vizierate administrative professionalization: Islamic history's first vizier system, Diwan departmentalization (tax/military/post/judicial)
Fiqh legislation & judicial independence: Qadi appointment/removal by Caliph but judgment per fiqh non-interferable, four madhhabs compete & flourish
Treasury centralization & currency reform: Dinar/Dirham standardization, land tax (kharaj)/poll tax (jizya) systematized
Translation movement & knowledge empire: Bayt al-Hikma (House of Wisdom) translates Greek/Persian/Indian learning, Arabic becomes scientific lingua franca
IQ-CAL-001.expected_en: Early Islamic empire achieves trans-ethnic/trans-linguistic/trans-civilizational mega-scale knowledge-political integration via trinity of 'fiqh constitution + scholar bureaucracy + translation movement', governance model lasts 500 years.
IQ-CAL-001.case_en: 762 Baghdad founded -> 786-809 Harun al-Rashid golden age -> 813-833 Al-Ma'mun/Al-Mu'tasim -> 945 Buyids seize real power -> 1258 Mongols sack Baghdad, caliphate nominal but fiqh governance legacy continues today.
IQ-CAL-001.intellectual_tradition: Abbasid Fiqh Governance / Islamic Legal Theory
IQ-CAL-001.cross_cultural_impact: Madhhab system for Islamic law; Bayt al-Hikma translation model; Diwan administrative template for Ottoman/Mughal/Safavid
IQ-CAL-001.resource_curse_mitigation: Bayt al-Mal fiscal discipline; waqf endowments for public goods; agricultural tax reform

IQ-NAT-001.name_en: Faisal I/Founding Fathers: Tribal Federal Governance & Iraqi State-Building
IQ-NAT-001.description_en: Faisal I (1885-1933), Hashemite, Arab Revolt leader, briefly King of Syria (1920), installed as Iraq's first King under British Mandate (1921-1933). Core governance challenge: supra-tribal/sectarian/ethnic state-building—Sunni/Shia/Kurd/Assyrian/Jewish/Mandaean coexistence. Mechanisms: tribal sheikhs into parliament/cabinet (tribal federalism), Sunni monarchy balances Shia majority (sectarian power-sharing), oil concession (1925 IPC) trades for infra/military modernization, 1930 Anglo-Iraqi Treaty exchanges nominal independence for League of Nations entry. Exemplifies M170 Tribal Federal Governance—tribal autonomy + nominal central sovereignty + external security umbrella, fragile equilibrium.
IQ-NAT-001.reason_en: Iraq's state-building is 'artificial borders + natural divisions' extreme puzzle: Sykes-Picot lines, three Ottoman vilayets (Baghdad/Basra/Mosul) forcibly merged. Faisal leverages Hashemite legitimacy + tribal federalism + diplomatic balancing to carve survival space among UK/France/Turkey/Iran/Saudi five-power squeeze. M170 distinct from M173 Hashemite Legitimacy (lineage) and M149 Islamic Shura (decision), core: 'tribal federalism as survival OS for artificial nation'.
steps_en: Hashemite legitimacy transplant: lost Syria -> installed in Iraq, lineage legitimacy cross-border transfer
Tribal federalism institutionalization: sheikhs in parliament/cabinet, tribal courts parallel state judiciary, revenue sharing
Sectarian balance art: Sunni monarchy/Shia majority/Kurdish autonomy, cabinet by sectarian quota (muhasasa prototype)
Oil for infra/military: 1925 IPC concession -> rail/road/Royal Iraqi Army, partial sovereignty exchange
